web.title: Ghat Ka Diya: Paper Boat Kitty Party Game Rules and Twists
web.description: Ghat Ka Diya is a team relay kitty party game: blow a paper boat with an LED diya across a parat of water with a straw. Rules, twists, tips and FAQs.
web.intro: Ghat Ka Diya is a team relay kitty party game where each lady blows a paper boat carrying an LED diya across a parat (wide steel tray) of water using only a straw, like floating a diya at the ghat. The first team whose every lady gets the boat across without the diya falling in wins. The twist is the Hawa card: each team can once make a lady from another team blow back against their boat for 5 seconds. It needs only a parat, paper, an LED tealight and straws, and suits 8 to 20 ladies in 10 to 15 minutes, especially around Chhath and Dev Diwali.
materials: One parat, big steel tray or plastic tub per team, filled with about 2 inches of water
Two folded paper boats per team, ideally made from glossy magazine pages
One battery operated LED tealight per team (never a real diya)
One straw per lady, so nobody shares
One paper card marked HAWA per team
An old bedsheet or towels under each parat to catch splashes
steps: Split the ladies into teams of 4 or 5. Place one parat of water on an old bedsheet for each team and mark a START side and a PAAR (finish) side.
Each team folds a paper boat and places a lit LED tealight in the middle of it.
The first lady puts the boat at START and blows it across to PAAR through her straw, without touching the boat or the water with her hands.
When the boat reaches PAAR, the next lady takes it back to START and blows it across, and so on down the team.
Any team can play its Hawa card once: a lady from that team stands at the PAAR side of another team's parat and blows the boat backwards through her straw for 5 seconds.
If the diya falls into the water or the boat sinks, that lady puts the boat back at START and tries again. Spare boats are allowed if one gets soggy.
rules: Hands may not touch the boat or the water. If they do, the boat goes back to START.
If the LED diya falls into the water, the current lady restarts from START.
Each team has one Hawa card, usable only once, for exactly 5 seconds against one other team.
The first team whose every lady has blown the boat across to PAAR wins and is crowned Ghat ki Rani.
variations: Pankha mode: instead of a straw, fan the boat across with a folded paper or a small hand fan.
Song mode: everyone hums "Kaagaz ki kashti" while blowing, and stopping the tune means a 3 second pause.
Final round: one lady from each team steers two boats at once with one straw.
tips: Use only LED tealights. Never put a real lit diya or candle on a paper boat indoors.
Fold boats from glossy magazine pages or rub a wax crayon on the bottom so they stay afloat longer.
Give every lady her own straw for hygiene, and keep spare boats ready.
Use shallow water and a sheet underneath so the floor stays dry and nobody slips.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Ghat Ka Diya?
faq.a: At least 2 teams of 4. With 8 to 20 ladies, make 2 to 4 teams of 4 or 5, each with its own parat, and the game takes 10 to 15 minutes.

faq.q: What do you need to play Ghat Ka Diya?
faq.a: A parat or tub of shallow water and two paper boats per team, one LED tealight per team, a straw for every lady, a Hawa card per team and an old sheet for the floor.

faq.q: Is Ghat Ka Diya a good Chhath or Dev Diwali kitty game?
faq.a: Yes. It recreates floating a diya on water at the ghat in a safe, indoor way, so it fits Chhath, Kartik Purnima and Dev Diwali kitties.

faq.q: How does the Hawa card work?
faq.a: Each team gets one card. When played, a lady from that team blows against another team's boat from the finish side for 5 seconds, pushing it back.

faq.q: Is Ghat Ka Diya safe to play indoors?
faq.a: Yes, if you use only battery LED tealights, keep the water about 2 inches deep and put a sheet or towels under each parat so the floor does not get slippery.
